1	"""Shared fixtures and the ``compare_screenshot`` helper for visual tests.
2	
3	Visual regression testing captures a screenshot of a GUI component and
4	compares it pixel-for-pixel against a committed *golden* reference image.
5	The test fails when the difference exceeds a threshold, which catches
6	unintended layout/paint changes that ordinary assertions miss.
7	
8	Capture works for two kinds of targets:
9	
10	* ``QWidget`` (e.g. ``MainWindow``, ``CanvasView``) — grabbed with
11	  ``QWidget.grab()``.
12	* ``QGraphicsItem`` (the hardware blocks) — blocks are scene items, not
13	  widgets, so they have no ``grab()``/``show()``. They are rendered through
14	  a ``QGraphicsScene`` instead.
15	
16	The first run auto-creates any missing golden, so a fresh test passes once
17	and then guards against regressions on every later run.
18	"""
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	import os
21	from pathlib import Path
22	
23	import numpy as np
24	import pytest
25	from PIL import Image, ImageChops
26	from PyQt6.QtCore import QRectF, Qt
27	from PyQt6.QtGui import QImage, QPainter
28	from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QGraphicsItem, QGraphicsScene, QWidget
29	
30	GOLDEN_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "golden"
31	DIFF_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "diffs"
32	DIFF_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
33	
34	# Max allowed RMS pixel difference (0-255 per channel, averaged over the
35	# image). 0 = pixel perfect; 5 tolerates minor antialiasing/font differences
36	# between machines without hiding real layout changes.
37	DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 5
38	
39	
40	@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
41	def qapp():
42	    """Single QApplication for the whole test session.
43	
44	    The repository's top-level ``tests/conftest.py`` forces
45	    ``QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`` before any Qt import, so this works
46	    headlessly (CI/EC2) with no display.
47	    """
48	    app = QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
49	    yield app
50	
51	
52	def _qimage_to_pil(qimage: QImage) -> Image.Image:
53	    """Convert a ``QImage`` to a PIL RGB image.
54	
55	    Converting to RGBA8888 first gives a known channel order and a tightly
56	    packed buffer (no row padding), so the same code works regardless of the
57	    platform's native pixmap format.
58	    """
59	    qimage = qimage.convertToFormat(QImage.Format.Format_RGBA8888)
60	    width, height = qimage.width(), qimage.height()
61	    ptr = qimage.bits()
62	    ptr.setsize(qimage.sizeInBytes())
63	    arr = np.frombuffer(ptr, dtype=np.uint8).reshape((height, width, 4))
64	    return Image.fromarray(arr, mode="RGBA").convert("RGB")
65	
66	
67	def _capture_graphics_item(item: QGraphicsItem) -> QImage:
68	    """Render a single ``QGraphicsItem`` (a hardware block) to a ``QImage``.
69	
70	    The item is rendered alone on a white background so the golden captures
71	    just the block — not the canvas grid or any neighbouring blocks. A
72	    detached item is parked in a temporary plain scene for the render and
73	    removed again afterwards so the caller's object is left untouched.
74	    """
75	    temp_scene = None
76	    scene = item.scene()
77	    if scene is None:
78	        temp_scene = QGraphicsScene()
79	        temp_scene.addItem(item)
80	        scene = temp_scene
81	
82	    source = item.mapToScene(item.boundingRect()).boundingRect()
83	    width, height = int(source.width()), int(source.height())
84	    image = QImage(width, height, QImage.Format.Format_ARGB32)
85	    image.fill(Qt.GlobalColor.white)
86	
87	    painter = QPainter(image)
88	    painter.setRenderHint(QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing)
89	    scene.render(painter, QRectF(0, 0, width, height), source)
90	    painter.end()
91	
92	    if temp_scene is not None:
93	        temp_scene.removeItem(item)
94	    return image
95	
96	
97	def _capture(target) -> QImage:
98	    """Capture a screenshot of a QWidget or a QGraphicsItem."""
99	    if isinstance(target, QWidget):
100	        return target.grab().toImage()
101	    if isinstance(target, QGraphicsItem):
102	        return _capture_graphics_item(target)
103	    raise TypeError(
104	        f"compare_screenshot expects a QWidget or QGraphicsItem, got {type(target)!r}"
105	    )
106	
107	
108	def compare_screenshot(target, name: str,
109	                       threshold: int = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
110	                       update_golden: bool = False) -> None:
111	    """Screenshot ``target`` and assert it matches ``golden/<name>.png``.
112	
113	    Args:
114	        target:        a ``QWidget`` or ``QGraphicsItem`` to screenshot.
115	        name:          golden filename stem, e.g. ``"main_window"``.
116	        threshold:     max allowed RMS pixel difference (default 5).
117	        update_golden: force-save the screenshot as the new golden. Also
118	                       triggered by the ``UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`` environment
119	                       variable so references can be refreshed in bulk after
120	                       an intentional UI change.
121	
122	    The golden is auto-created when missing (first run), so a new test passes
123	    once and then guards against regressions. On failure the actual and an
124	    amplified diff image are written to ``tests/visual/diffs/`` and the
125	    assertion message explains how to accept the change.
126	    """
127	    golden_path = GOLDEN_DIR / f"{name}.png"
128	    diff_path = DIFF_DIR / f"{name}_diff.png"
129	    actual_path = DIFF_DIR / f"{name}_actual.png"
130	
131	    update_golden = update_golden or os.environ.get("UPDATE_GOLDEN", "0") == "1"
132	
133	    actual = _qimage_to_pil(_capture(target))
134	
135	    if update_golden or not golden_path.exists():
136	        GOLDEN_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
137	        actual.save(golden_path)
138	        print(f"Golden image saved: {golden_path}")
139	        return
140	
141	    golden = Image.open(golden_path).convert("RGB")
142	
143	    assert actual.size == golden.size, (
144	        f"Screenshot size changed: expected {golden.size}, got {actual.size}.\n"
145	        f"If intentional, delete {golden_path} and re-run to regenerate."
146	    )
147	
148	    diff = ImageChops.difference(actual, golden)
149	    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.asarray(diff, dtype=float) ** 2)))
150	
151	    if rms > threshold:
152	        actual.save(actual_path)
153	        # Amplify the diff 10x so small differences are visible to a human.
154	        amplified = Image.fromarray(
155	            np.clip(np.asarray(diff) * 10, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
156	        )
157	        amplified.save(diff_path)
158	        raise AssertionError(
159	            f"Visual regression: '{name}' pixel RMS={rms:.2f} > threshold={threshold}\n"
160	            f"  Golden: {golden_path}\n"
161	            f"  Actual: {actual_path}\n"
162	            f"  Diff:   {diff_path}  (amplified 10x)\n"
163	            f"If intentional: review the actual image, then\n"
164	            f"  cp {actual_path} {golden_path} && git add {golden_path}"
165	        )
166	
167	    print(f"Visual OK: '{name}' RMS={rms:.2f} (threshold={threshold})")
168

1	"""Visual + smoke tests for the Silmulator main window.
2	
3	These run headlessly: the repository's top-level ``tests/conftest.py`` sets
4	``QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`` before Qt is imported, and on EC2 pytest-xvfb
5	provides a virtual display, so no ``DISPLAY`` needs to be set by hand.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from silmulator.gui.main_window import MainWindow
10	
11	from .conftest import compare_screenshot
12	
13	# The window resizes itself to 1400x900; it must never render smaller than
14	# this usable minimum or docks/toolbar controls get clipped.
15	MIN_WIDTH = 800
16	MIN_HEIGHT = 600
17	
18	
19	def test_main_window_opens(qapp, qtbot):
20	    """Main window renders without crashing and matches the golden image."""
21	    window = MainWindow()
22	    qtbot.addWidget(window)
23	    window.show()
24	    qtbot.waitExposed(window, timeout=5000)
25	    qapp.processEvents()  # flush pending layout/paint events before grabbing
26	    compare_screenshot(window, "main_window")
27	
28	
29	def test_main_window_title(qapp, qtbot):
30	    """Window title identifies the app.
31	
32	    The issue specifies ``== "Silmulator"``, but the real window appends a
33	    subtitle (``"Silmulator — SIL/HIL/CIL Hardware Simulator"``). Asserting
34	    the prefix honours the intent (the window is identifiably Silmulator)
35	    without coupling the test to the exact subtitle wording.
36	    """
37	    window = MainWindow()
38	    qtbot.addWidget(window)
39	    assert window.windowTitle().startswith("Silmulator")
40	
41	
42	def test_main_window_minimum_size(qapp, qtbot):
43	    """Window opens at least 800x600 so no controls are clipped."""
44	    window = MainWindow()
45	    qtbot.addWidget(window)
46	    window.show()
47	    qtbot.waitExposed(window, timeout=5000)
48	    qapp.processEvents()
49	    assert window.width() >= MIN_WIDTH
50	    assert window.height() >= MIN_HEIGHT
51

1	"""Visual tests: every built-in hardware block renders correctly.
2	
3	Blocks are ``QGraphicsItem``s, not ``QWidget``s, so they cannot be
4	``show()``/``waitExposed``-ed like the main window — ``compare_screenshot``
5	renders them through a ``QGraphicsScene`` instead (see conftest). Each block
6	is captured in its default, unconfigured state.
7	
8	One golden per block type. Parametrised over the built-in types (following
9	the existing pattern in ``tests/test_block_creation.py``) so adding a new
10	built-in block automatically gets a render test once it is listed here.
11	"""
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import pytest
15	
16	from silmulator.gui.canvas import BLOCK_REGISTRY
17	
18	from .conftest import compare_screenshot
19	
20	# device_type (registry key) -> golden image stem.
21	BUILTIN_BLOCKS = {
22	    "Oscilloscope": "oscilloscope_block",
23	    "Power Supply": "psu_block",
24	    "Function Generator": "function_generator_block",
25	    "Multimeter": "multimeter_block",
26	    "MSP430": "msp430_block",
27	    "Code Input": "code_input_block",
28	}
29	
30	
31	# A fixed value to substitute for any live, noisy instrument reading so the
32	# golden is reproducible. The multimeter, for instance, adds random Gaussian
33	# noise to every reading it paints.
34	FROZEN_READING = 1.2345678
35	
36	
37	def _freeze_live_readings(block) -> None:
38	    """Replace a device's noisy ``_get_reading`` with a constant.
39	
40	    Without this, blocks that paint a fresh measurement (e.g. the multimeter)
41	    render differently on every capture and can never match a golden.
42	    """
43	    device = getattr(block, "device", None)
44	    if hasattr(device, "_get_reading"):
45	        device._get_reading = lambda func=None: FROZEN_READING
46	
47	
48	@pytest.mark.parametrize("device_type,golden", list(BUILTIN_BLOCKS.items()))
49	def test_block_renders(qapp, device_type, golden):
50	    """Each built-in block renders to its golden image in default state."""
51	    cls = BLOCK_REGISTRY.get(device_type)
52	    if cls is None:
53	        pytest.skip(f"block type {device_type!r} not registered")
54	    block = cls()
55	    _freeze_live_readings(block)
56	    qapp.processEvents()
57	    compare_screenshot(block, golden)
58

1	"""Visual + interaction tests for the canvas.
2	
3	``test_canvas_with_psu_block`` is a real interaction test: it clicks the
4	"Power Supply" button via ``qtbot.mouseClick`` and waits for the block to
5	appear with ``qtbot.waitUntil`` (never ``time.sleep``), exactly as a user
6	would add a block.
7	
8	Note on what "the device palette" is: the GUI exposes block-adding in two
9	places — a toolbar with one ``QPushButton`` per block type, and a dockable
10	library list (double-click). These tests drive the toolbar button.
11	
12	The canvas auto-places a new block at the far top-left of the (large) scene,
13	which is off-screen in the default view, so the test calls the app's own
14	``fit_all()`` to bring the block into view before screenshotting — otherwise
15	the golden would show an empty viewport.
16	"""
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt
20	from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QPushButton
21	
22	from silmulator.gui.main_window import MainWindow
23	
24	from .conftest import compare_screenshot
25	
26	# Fixed window size so the canvas viewport geometry — and therefore the
27	# background grid and fitted block — render identically on every machine.
28	WINDOW_WIDTH = 1000
29	WINDOW_HEIGHT = 700
30	WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000
31	
32	
33	def _find_palette_button(window: MainWindow, label: str) -> QPushButton:
34	    """Return the toolbar button that adds the given block type."""
35	    for button in window.findChildren(QPushButton):
36	        if button.text() == label:
37	            return button

3	The GUI is covered by **visual regression tests**: each test captures a
4	screenshot of a component and compares it pixel-for-pixel against a committed
5	*golden* reference image. A test fails when the difference exceeds a small
6	threshold, catching layout and paint regressions that ordinary assertions miss.
7	
8	Tests live in `tests/visual/`. The shared helper is `compare_screenshot()` in
9	`tests/visual/conftest.py`.
10	
11	## Running the tests
12	
13	Everything runs in one command — visual tests are included automatically:
14	
15	```bash
16	pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
17	pytest tests/ -v
18	```

20	**No `DISPLAY` and no `xvfb-run` prefix are required.** The repository's
21	top-level `tests/conftest.py` sets `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` before Qt is
22	imported, so Qt renders to an in-memory surface. On CI/EC2, `pytest-xvfb`
23	additionally starts a virtual X framebuffer automatically when the package is
24	installed. You never set `DISPLAY` by hand.
25	
26	To run only the visual tests:

29	pytest tests/visual/ -v
30	```

32	## How golden images work
33	
34	- Golden images live in `tests/visual/golden/` and **are committed** — they are
35	  the ground truth.
36	- On the **first** run of a new test, the golden is missing, so it is generated
37	  and saved automatically and the test passes. Commit the new golden.
38	- On **every later** run, the screenshot is compared against the golden and the
39	  test fails if the RMS pixel difference exceeds the threshold (default `5`).
40	- Diagnostic images go to `tests/visual/diffs/` and `tests/visual/actual/`,
41	  which are **git-ignored** — never commit them.
42	
43	## Updating golden images after an intentional UI change
44	
45	When you change the UI on purpose, the old goldens no longer match. Update them:
46	
47	```bash
48	# Update one golden: delete it and re-run the test to regenerate
49	rm tests/visual/golden/main_window.png

Silmulator / Lesson 0008 — Visual Regression Testing

Visual Regression Testing

Why this matters: the Silmulator GUI draws hardware faces (LCD readouts, waveform previews, port layouts) with raw QPainter calls. No unit assertion can tell you the multimeter's LCD shifted three pixels or the PSU header lost its colour. A golden-image test catches exactly that class of silent visual regression.

§0 Why visual regression testing

Ordinary tests assert on values: assert window.windowTitle().startswith("Silmulator"). They are blind to how something looks. A block can render with the wrong colour, a clipped label, or a misplaced port, and every value-based assertion will still pass.

A visual regression test captures a screenshot of a GUI component and compares it pixel-for-pixel against a committed reference image — the golden. The test fails when the difference exceeds a threshold.

What it catchesValue assertionGolden image
Wrong window title string✓~
Block header colour changed✗✓
LCD readout shifted / clipped✗✓
Port moved to wrong edge✗✓
Toolbar control disappeared after a paint change✗✓
Numeric simulation result✓✗

The two are complementary. test_gui_main_window.py keeps both side by side: test_main_window_title asserts the title string, while test_main_window_opens calls compare_screenshot(window, "main_window") to guard the rendering.

Golden-image concept: the golden is the single ground truth of "what the UI is supposed to look like." It is committed to git. Every later test run re-renders the same component and diffs against it. A diff over threshold means either you broke something, or you changed the UI on purpose and need to refresh the golden.

§1 The compare_screenshot helper

tests/visual/conftest.py

One function does the whole job: compare_screenshot(target, name, threshold=DEFAULT_THRESHOLD, update_golden=False). Its pipeline is capture → convert → compare → threshold.

def compare_screenshot(target, name: str,
                       threshold: int = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
                       update_golden: bool = False) -> None:
    golden_path = GOLDEN_DIR / f"{name}.png"
    diff_path   = DIFF_DIR / f"{name}_diff.png"
    actual_path = DIFF_DIR / f"{name}_actual.png"

    update_golden = update_golden or os.environ.get("UPDATE_GOLDEN", "0") == "1"

    actual = _qimage_to_pil(_capture(target))   ← capture + convert to PIL RGB

    if update_golden or not golden_path.exists():
        GOLDEN_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        actual.save(golden_path)            ← FIRST RUN: auto-create golden, pass
        return

    golden = Image.open(golden_path).convert("RGB")

    assert actual.size == golden.size, ...   ← size mismatch is its own clear error

    diff = ImageChops.difference(actual, golden)
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.asarray(diff, dtype=float) ** 2)))

    if rms > threshold:                      ← over threshold → FAIL + write diagnostics
        actual.save(actual_path)
        amplified = Image.fromarray(
            np.clip(np.asarray(diff) * 10, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8))
        amplified.save(diff_path)        ← diff amplified 10x so it's visible
        raise AssertionError(...)

The four stages

capture _capture(target) returns a QImage — branching on whether the target is a QWidget or a QGraphicsItem (covered in §2). convert _qimage_to_pil() converts the QImage to Format_RGBA8888 first (known channel order, no row padding), wraps the buffer in a NumPy array, then returns a PIL image converted to "RGB". compare ImageChops.difference(actual, golden) produces a per-pixel difference image. The metric is RMS: sqrt(mean(diff**2)) over every channel of every pixel. threshold If rms > threshold the test fails. DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 5.

Auto-create on first run

The key behaviour that makes this painless: if update_golden or not golden_path.exists(): saves the screenshot as the golden and returns. So the very first time a new test runs, the golden is missing, it gets created, and the test passes. Every later run compares against it. You write the test once and get regression protection forever — you just commit the generated golden.

Diagnostics on failure

When the RMS exceeds threshold, two files land in tests/visual/diffs/: <name>_actual.png (what this run rendered) and <name>_diff.png (the difference, multiplied by 10 so a 2-pixel-value drift becomes visible to a human). The AssertionError message prints all three paths plus the exact cp ... && git add ... command to accept the change if it was intentional.

Size mismatch is special. Before computing the RMS, the helper asserts actual.size == golden.size. ImageChops.difference requires equal dimensions, so a changed window/block size gets its own clear message ("Screenshot size changed: expected ..., got ...") instead of a confusing crash.

§2 Capturing two kinds of targets

tests/visual/conftest.py — _capture(), _capture_graphics_item()

Silmulator's GUI has two fundamentally different visual objects, and they are captured differently:

TargetExamplesHow captured
QWidgetMainWindow, CanvasViewtarget.grab().toImage()
QGraphicsItemevery hardware blockrendered through a QGraphicsScene
def _capture(target) -> QImage:
    if isinstance(target, QWidget):
        return target.grab().toImage()        ← widgets can grab themselves
    if isinstance(target, QGraphicsItem):
        return _capture_graphics_item(target)
    raise TypeError(...)                     ← anything else is a usage error

Why blocks can't .show() / .grab()

Hardware blocks (MultimeterBlock, PowerSupplyBlock, …) inherit from BaseBlock, which is a QGraphicsItem — not a QWidget. QGraphicsItem has no show() and no grab(): an item only exists inside a scene, it is not a standalone window. So compare_screenshot(block, ...) takes the scene path.

Rendering an item through a scene

def _capture_graphics_item(item: QGraphicsItem) -> QImage:
    temp_scene = None
    scene = item.scene()
    if scene is None:                       ← detached item? park it in a temp scene
        temp_scene = QGraphicsScene()
        temp_scene.addItem(item)
        scene = temp_scene

    source = item.mapToScene(item.boundingRect()).boundingRect()
    width, height = int(source.width()), int(source.height())
    image = QImage(width, height, QImage.Format.Format_ARGB32)
    image.fill(Qt.GlobalColor.white)        ← white bg, NOT the canvas grid

    painter = QPainter(image)
    painter.setRenderHint(QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing)
    scene.render(painter, QRectF(0, 0, width, height), source)
    painter.end()

    if temp_scene is not None:
        temp_scene.removeItem(item)             ← leave caller's object untouched
    return image

Three things to notice:

  • White background, isolated item. The item is rendered alone on a white fill, so the golden captures just the block — not the canvas grid or neighbouring blocks. That keeps a block golden stable even when the canvas around it changes.
  • Detached items are handled. If the block isn't in a scene yet (item.scene() is None), it is temporarily added to a throwaway QGraphicsScene for the render and removed afterward, so the caller's object is left exactly as it was.
  • Bounding-rect crop. source is the item's bounding rect mapped to scene coordinates, so the captured image is exactly block-sized.
test_gui_blocks.py uses the item path; test_gui_main_window.py (the window) and test_gui_canvas.py (window.canvas_view) use the widget path. Same helper, two branches.

§3 Determinism — making renders reproducible

A golden test is only useful if the same component renders identically every run. Anything random, machine-dependent, or off-screen breaks that. Silmulator handles four sources of non-determinism.

1. Threshold = 5, not 0

Font hinting and antialiasing differ slightly between machines and Qt builds. A threshold of 0 (pixel-perfect) would make tests flaky across environments. DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 5 absorbs sub-pixel rendering noise while still catching real layout changes. The RMS is a per-channel value on the 0–255 scale, averaged over the whole image — so a small antialiasing wiggle stays under 5, but a moved label or recoloured header blows past it.

2. Freezing the multimeter's random reading

The multimeter device computes its reading as base + random.gauss(0, noise) — it paints a fresh, noisy value every time. That reading would differ on every capture and could never match a golden. test_gui_blocks.py monkeypatches it to a constant:

FROZEN_READING = 1.2345678

def _freeze_live_readings(block) -> None:
    device = getattr(block, "device", None)
    if hasattr(device, "_get_reading"):
        device._get_reading = lambda func=None: FROZEN_READING

Any device that exposes _get_reading gets it replaced with a lambda returning FROZEN_READING. The block then paints a stable value, so its golden is reproducible. Devices without _get_reading are left untouched (the hasattr guard).

3. Fixed window size

test_gui_canvas.py resizes the window to a constant WINDOW_WIDTH = 1000, WINDOW_HEIGHT = 700 before screenshotting. The canvas viewport geometry — and therefore the background grid and the fitted block — then render identically on every machine. Without a fixed size, the golden would depend on whatever default size each environment chose.

4. fit_all() for off-screen blocks

The canvas auto-places a new block at the far top-left of the large scene, which is off-screen in the default view. If you screenshot the viewport then, the golden would just show an empty grid. The interaction test clicks the toolbar button, waits for the block, then calls the app's own fit_all() to bring it into view:

psu_button = _find_palette_button(window, "Power Supply")
qtbot.mouseClick(psu_button, Qt.MouseButton.LeftButton)

qtbot.waitUntil(lambda: len(window.canvas.blocks) == 1, timeout=WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS)

window.canvas_view.fit_all()        ← bring the auto-placed block into view
qapp.processEvents()
compare_screenshot(window.canvas_view, "canvas_with_psu_block")
Never use time.sleep() to wait for the GUI. The tests use qtbot.waitUntil(lambda: len(window.canvas.blocks) == 1) and qtbot.waitExposed(window) — they block until the condition is actually true (or time out), which is both faster and not flaky. A fixed sleep is either too short (flaky) or too slow (wasteful). Also call qapp.processEvents() to flush pending layout/paint events before grabbing.

§4 The update-golden workflow

docs/visual-testing.md

When you change the UI on purpose, the old goldens no longer match and the tests fail — correctly. You then refresh the goldens. Two ways:

# Update ONE golden: delete it and re-run; the helper auto-recreates it
rm tests/visual/golden/main_window.png
pytest tests/visual/test_gui_main_window.py::test_main_window_opens

# Update EVERY golden at once via the env var
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pytest tests/visual/

Both routes go through the same branch in compare_screenshot: if update_golden or not golden_path.exists(). Deleting the file makes exists() false; UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 sets the flag directly. Either way the current render is saved as the new golden and the test passes.

Review before you commit. A golden update is only correct if the new rendering is what you intended. Open <name>_actual.png (or the regenerated golden) and eyeball it. A blindly accepted golden silently bakes in whatever regression you were supposed to catch — the test will then "pass" forever on the bug.

What's committed vs ignored

PathCommitted?Role
tests/visual/golden/✓ committedground truth references
tests/visual/diffs/✗ git-ignoredper-run diagnostics (actual + amplified diff)
git add tests/visual/golden/
git commit -m "chore(visual): update goldens after <describe UI change>"
Mental model: goldens are source — they live in git and change deliberately through review. Diffs are artifacts — generated on failure, never committed, safe to delete anytime.

§5 Headless execution

These are GUI tests, but they run with no display — locally, in CI, and on the overnight EC2 runner. You never set DISPLAY by hand and never prefix with xvfb-run. Two pieces make that work.

1. QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen

The repository's top-level tests/conftest.py sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen before any Qt module is imported. That tells Qt to render to an in-memory surface instead of a real window server. Ordering matters: the variable must be set before Qt reads it at import time, which is exactly why it lives in the top-level conftest rather than inside a test.

The session-scoped qapp fixture then just constructs the single application:

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def qapp():
    app = QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    yield app

One QApplication for the whole session (you can only have one), reused if some other fixture already made one.

2. pytest-xvfb on EC2

On a fresh headless Linux box, pytest-xvfb additionally starts a virtual X framebuffer automatically when the package is installed (it's in requirements-dev.txt). Combined with offscreen rendering, that means the full GUI suite runs with a plain:

pytest tests/ -v          # visual tests included automatically, no DISPLAY

A one-time ./scripts/setup-visual-testing.sh installs the system-level xvfb and Qt XCB runtime libraries via apt-get. After that, every checkout just needs pip install -r requirements-dev.txt.

Generate goldens on the same platform the tests run on. Because rendering differs slightly between platforms, goldens created on the EC2 runner match most closely there. If you generate a golden on macOS and run the test on Linux, even threshold=5 may not absorb the difference.

§6 Practice

Quick-fire quiz

Q1. The first time a brand-new visual test runs, no golden file exists yet. What does compare_screenshot do?
  • It raises an AssertionError saying the golden is missing, so you must generate it manually first.
  • It saves the current screenshot as golden/<name>.png, prints a message, and returns — the test passes.
  • It skips the test with pytest.skip until a golden has been committed.
  • It compares the render against an all-white blank image and passes if the block is mostly white.
Q2. A hardware block is a QGraphicsItem, not a QWidget. Why can't compare_screenshot just call block.grab() like it does for the main window?
  • A QGraphicsItem has no grab() (or show()) method — it only exists inside a scene, so it is rendered via QGraphicsScene.render() instead.
  • Blocks have a grab() method but it is too slow, so the scene-render path is used for speed.
  • Blocks' grab() returns a transparent image, so a white background must be added by rendering through a scene.
  • There is no real difference — both call grab(); _capture_graphics_item is just a thin alias.
Q3. Why is DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 5 instead of 0 (pixel-perfect)?
  • Blocks use colours within 5 units of each other, so anything tighter would confuse adjacent shades.
  • Font hinting and antialiasing differ between machines/Qt builds; threshold 0 would be flaky, while 5 absorbs sub-pixel noise but still catches real changes.
  • 5 means 5% of pixels are allowed to differ completely before the test fails.
  • PNG compression introduces up to 5 units of loss, so the threshold compensates for it.
Q4. The multimeter block paints a reading computed as base + random.gauss(0, noise). Without intervention, what happens to its golden test, and how is it fixed?
  • It would render a different value every run and could never match the golden; _freeze_live_readings replaces device._get_reading with a lambda returning a constant.
  • The threshold of 5 absorbs the small noise, so no fix is needed.
  • A fixed random seed is set in conftest so random.gauss returns the same value each run.
  • The multimeter test is skipped because noisy instruments can't be visually tested.
Q5. In test_canvas_with_psu_block, after clicking the PSU button and waiting for the block, why does the test call window.canvas_view.fit_all() before the screenshot?
  • It clears any leftover blocks from a previous test so the canvas starts clean.
  • The block is auto-placed off-screen at the far top-left of the scene; fit_all() brings it into the viewport, otherwise the golden would show an empty grid.
  • It forces an immediate synchronous repaint that qapp.processEvents() can't trigger.
  • It resizes the block to a standard size so the golden dimensions are stable.
Q6. You intentionally changed the PSU header colour. The visual test now fails. What is the correct way to make it green again, and what must you do before committing?
  • Bump threshold for that test high enough that the new colour passes against the old golden.
  • Open the golden PNG in an image editor and recolour the header to match.
  • Regenerate the golden (delete it and rerun, or UPDATE_GOLDEN=1), then review the new image before git add.
  • Commit the generated diffs/<name>_actual.png as the new reference.
Q7. How do these GUI tests run on the headless EC2 runner with no DISPLAY set?
  • The top-level conftest.py sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen before Qt is imported, and pytest-xvfb starts a virtual framebuffer automatically.
  • Qt is mocked out entirely, so no real rendering happens; the goldens are synthetic.
  • Each test must be launched with an xvfb-run prefix; the CI script adds it.
  • The qapp fixture sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen right before creating the QApplication.
Q8. When a comparison fails because the component changed size, what does compare_screenshot do differently from a normal pixel-difference failure?
  • It scales the actual image down to the golden's size, then computes the RMS as usual.
  • It asserts actual.size == golden.size first and raises a specific 'Screenshot size changed' message before any RMS is computed.
  • It auto-updates the golden to the new size since size changes are always intentional.
  • It crops the larger image to the smaller one's bounding box and compares the overlap.
0 / 8 answered

Scenario questions

You add a new SignalGeneratorBlock and want a visual test for it. Walk through what you write, what happens on the first pytest run, and what you commit.
Add the block to BUILTIN_BLOCKS in test_gui_blocks.py mapping its registry key to a golden stem (e.g. "Signal Generator": "signal_generator_block"). The parametrised test_block_renders instantiates it, calls _freeze_live_readings, and calls compare_screenshot(block, "signal_generator_block"). First run: golden/signal_generator_block.png doesn't exist, so compare_screenshot saves the render and returns — test passes. You then OPEN the generated PNG to confirm it looks right, and git add tests/visual/golden/signal_generator_block.png. Every later run diffs against it.
A teammate's multimeter visual test passes on their Mac but fails on the EC2 runner with RMS just above 5. Diagnose and give the fix.
The golden was generated on macOS but the test runs on Linux; font hinting and antialiasing differ between platforms, pushing the RMS just over the threshold of 5. The fix is to generate goldens on the same platform the tests run on — regenerate the golden on the EC2 runner (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pytest, or delete + rerun there), review it, and commit that version. (Do NOT just raise the threshold — that weakens regression protection. The doc explicitly says to generate goldens on the target platform.)
Explain, in order, the four stages compare_screenshot performs on a normal (golden-exists) run, naming the key function or operation at each stage.
(1) Capture: _capture(target) → QImage, branching on QWidget (target.grab().toImage()) vs QGraphicsItem (_capture_graphics_item via QGraphicsScene.render). (2) Convert: _qimage_to_pil() converts to Format_RGBA8888, wraps the buffer in a NumPy array, returns a PIL "RGB" image. (3) Compare: assert sizes equal, then ImageChops.difference(actual, golden) and rms = sqrt(mean(diff**2)). (4) Threshold: if rms > threshold, save actual + 10x-amplified diff into diffs/ and raise AssertionError with the cp/git-add hint; otherwise pass.
Why does _capture_graphics_item create a temporary QGraphicsScene when item.scene() is None, and why does it remove the item again at the end?
A QGraphicsItem can only be rendered through a scene — scene.render() does the painting. If the block isn't attached to a scene yet (item.scene() is None, e.g. it was just constructed by the parametrised test), there's nothing to render through, so the helper parks it in a throwaway QGraphicsScene. It removes the item again (temp_scene.removeItem(item)) so the caller's object is left exactly as it was found — no surprise side effects of having been captured. Items that already belong to a scene are rendered in place and not removed.
Your CI shows a visual failure. The artifacts you need to diagnose it live in tests/visual/diffs/, but that directory is git-ignored. How do you actually look at them, and which file shows you where the change is?
diffs/ is git-ignored because it's per-run diagnostic output, not source — so it won't be in the repo, you retrieve it from the CI job's artifacts (or reproduce the failure locally and look in tests/visual/diffs/). Two files are written on failure: <name>_actual.png (what this run rendered) and <name>_diff.png (the per-pixel difference amplified 10x). The amplified _diff.png is the one that shows WHERE they differ — small drifts become visibly bright. Compare _actual.png against the committed golden/<name>.png side by side to see what changed.
Why must QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen be set in the top-level tests/conftest.py rather than inside the qapp fixture?
Qt reads QT_QPA_PLATFORM when its modules are first imported and the platform plugin is selected. By the time the qapp fixture runs, Qt (PyQt6) has already been imported — at the top of the test modules and conftest — so setting the variable there would be too late. The top-level conftest.py runs/sets it before any Qt import happens, guaranteeing Qt picks the offscreen platform plugin. This is the same 'set env before import' ordering rule that governs many Qt configuration knobs.
